# requires: logging
#
# One record travelling writer -> relay -> receiver, and the question the chain
# exists to answer: who wrote this, and who handed it to me. With one verified
# field the second stamp overwrites the first and the author disappears; with a
# chain both are on the record, and what each is worth is the receiver's
# assessment, never the wire's.
#
# Nothing here opens a socket. `attest` applies what a receiving service does
# when the platform's attester answered with that mechanism, and keeps the
# stamp as the anchor the receiver assesses from; `send` hands the record to
# the next party, whose anchor it is not. `relay` on an attest means the party
# the receiver established is one its policy authorises to attest the hops
# beneath it.
#
# Step 10 is the whole ruling in one line: the stamp a real service made at
# step 5 arrives at the next receiver as an assertion, the same bytes a forgery
# would be, and it stands as vouched at step 12 only because the receiver
# established the party that carried it and its policy authorises that party.
record R 0
chain R
uid R 0
author R
attest R so_peercred
chain R
author R
relay R
send R
chain R
attest R so_peercred relay
chain R
author R
relay R
disputed R

# expect 2: ok 0:self:claimed [LOG-I1] [LOG-I2]
# expect 3: ok uid=-1 [LOG-I11]
# expect 4: no-answer unattributed [LOG-I9]
# expect 6: ok 0:self:claimed 1:so_peercred:established [LOG-I1] [LOG-I6] [LOG-I13]
# expect 7: ok by=so_peercred hop=1 [LOG-I7]
# expect 8: ok by=so_peercred hop=1 [LOG-I8]
# expect 10: ok 0:self:claimed 1:so_peercred:asserted [LOG-I5] [LOG-I13]
# expect 12: ok 0:self:claimed 1:so_peercred:vouched 2:so_peercred:established [LOG-I1] [LOG-I4] [LOG-I6] [LOG-I14]
# expect 13: ok by=so_peercred hop=1 [LOG-I7] [LOG-I14]
# expect 14: ok by=so_peercred hop=2 [LOG-I8]
# expect 15: ok disputed=no [LOG-I10]
